title: Choose the visual world — RetroMobi
question: Your brief pins Apple restraint, glass, the green Earth map and amber — those survive in every card. The roll decides what the brief leaves open: topology, controls, state vocabulary and ritual.

options.label: The Rental Register
options.lineage: RC books, workshop service records, the statutory rental register
options.thesis: Every claim on screen is a stamped entry: which authority licensed it, which number, valid until when.
options.viewport: The town's terrain fills the frame. One glass register panel sits over it, and the first scooter's row is already stamped — licence number, issuing authority, valid-to date — before any price is read.
options.risk: Goes bureaucratic the moment a stamp becomes decoration instead of a real record.

raised.raise: Every stacked offer is enumerated with its own values — depth never implies a count.
The landing page is one committed column in a chosen order, not a grid of equal sections.
Selection and focus are carried by luminance, not hue — which is what makes an amber pin survive green-brown terrain.
A date or filter change shows its consequence before it commits.

options.label: The Survey Sheet
options.thesis: The hills are the interface — contours, spot heights and a grid reference that names every shop.
options.viewport: A single topographic sheet of the town, shops plotted as surveyed points, the date window set in the sheet's margin legend.
options.risk: It is also where most runs land when a brief already pins a map — the familiar answer wearing good drafting.

options.label: The Fold Sequence
options.thesis: Booking as a numbered sequence of deliberate folds, every earlier crease still visible.
options.viewport: A strict margin column of numbered steps beside the live booking, one gold dot marking where you are.
options.case: Fuses strongly on product clarity — the funnel is irreversible steps, and constraint-aware folding maps exactly onto the licence gate. Loses audience identification: a Rishikesh renter does not live in origami.
options.risk: The step column becomes a progress bar wearing a costume if the earlier state is not genuinely still readable.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.lineage: a small aircraft's night instrument six-pack
options.thesis: Six gauges, each owning one truth, cross-checked in a fixed sweep before you commit.
options.viewport: Licence, documents, price, distance, rating and availability as six gauges that must agree before the book action lights.
options.case: Fuses strongly on product clarity — each gauge owning one truth is the cross-check a rental actually requires, and trend-before-alarm suits expiring documents. Loses on identification, and its amber is reserved for caution, colliding with your pinned accent.
options.risk: A dial that shows a number a label could have shown is instrument cosplay.

options.label: Registered Colour Passes
options.thesis: Offers as registered spot-colour layers that mix where they overlap.
options.viewport: Each shop's offer as its own colour pass over one model.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a renter does not identify with printmaking, and overlap obscures the price it should clarify.
options.kept: Every stacked layer is named with its values, never implied by depth.
options.risk: Overlap reads as noise the moment more than three offers stack.

options.label: The Shrine Page
options.thesis: One long devoted column carrying somebody's entire enthusiasm in their chosen order.
options.viewport: A centred fixed-width column, each section closed by a divider.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a fixed-width table that refuses to adapt is disqualifying for a phone-first product with a legal accessibility duty.
options.kept: One committed column in a chosen order, not a grid of equal sections.
options.risk: Nostalgia with no mechanism underneath it.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Attention itself is the illumination model — what you approach lights up.
options.viewport: Paths revealing by proximity glow, destinations announcing as distant pulses.
options.case: Fuses poorly: near-black bioluminescence cannot carry a daylight outdoor product with a 7:1 contrast need, and it has no vocabulary for a licence or a price.
options.kept: Focus carried by luminance rather than hue — the fix for an amber pin on green-brown terrain.

options.label: The Source Floor
options.thesis: The source is the stage; edits apply on the next cycle boundary and are visible before they land.
options.viewport: One code buffer whose cursor line is the downbeat.
options.case: Fuses poorly: monospace-as-technical-costume is exactly what a first-time renter in a hill town cannot read.
options.kept: Pending changes are visible before they commit.
options.risk: Signals engineering to an audience that wants a scooter.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Zoomcar, Royal Brothers and Freedo ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Filter rail left, result cards centre, map right — the arrangement a visitor already expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
